bullets.title: ORCL freefall on $40B AI capex raise; Cramer says buy the dip
bullets.body: Oracle dropped 11%+ intraday after announcing plans to raise $40B to fund AI data center expansion. Jim Cramer publicly recommended buying the pullback, calling the selloff an overreaction to elevated but growth-oriented capex.

bullets.title: NVDA drives 14% of S&P 500 move; DLSS critical to Switch 2
bullets.body: NVDA accounted for 14% of the S&P 500's prior session move, underscoring its outsized index influence. Separately, NVIDIA's DLSS is described as the Switch 2's 'secret weapon'—without it, the system struggles to match PS4-level performance in games like Kingdom Hearts 3.

bullets.title: NVDA partners with Abridge on healthcare AI model
bullets.body: Nvidia announced a partnership with Abridge, an AI note-taking startup for doctors, to train a healthcare-specific AI model per WSJ. The deal extends NVDA's vertical AI application strategy beyond data center hardware.

bullets.title: GOOGL explores Samsung 2nm for TPU v10; may reduce TSMC share
bullets.body: Per The Information, Google is considering Samsung Foundry's 2nm process node for the I/O die of its TPU v10 'Icefish' chip. This would represent a meaningful diversification away from TSMC for advanced AI accelerator manufacturing.

bullets.title: GOOGL rejected Trump administration quantum computing funds over speed constraints
bullets.body: Google declined federal quantum computing subsidies because attached conditions would have slowed the company's development pace. Google prioritized autonomy and speed over the financial benefit of the subsidy.

bullets.title: GOOGL $80B issuance surge coincides with financial asset peak
bullets.body: One trader argues it is 'no coincidence' that financial assets in aggregate peaked when Google initiated an $80B new issuance. The thesis is that market absorption of such supply creates broad price pressure.

bullets.title: META ends Manus partnership after China regulatory demand
bullets.body: Meta terminated its partnership with AI startup Manus following demands from Chinese regulators to unwind the deal. No financial terms were disclosed.

bullets.title: MSFT restricts Claude Fable for employees over data retention
bullets.body: Microsoft has restricted employee access to Anthropic's Claude Fable product, citing data retention concerns. The move signals internal information-security friction with third-party AI tools even at an AI-investing hyperscaler.

bullets.title: MSFT back in Bill Ackman's buying zone
bullets.body: Commentary on social media notes MSFT has declined to a price level that Bill Ackman considers attractive for accumulation. No specific price or position size disclosed.

bullets.title: TTD competitive risk: Walmart expanding DSP partnerships
bullets.body: Walmart is embracing more demand-side platforms (DSPs), a dynamic that directly contradicts Trade Desk CEO Jeff Green's prior public statement that the competitive landscape is not intensifying. Flagged as a bearish signal for TTD's moat narrative.

bullets.title: AAOI positioned as domestic AI infrastructure champion; $471M/month revenue scenario by H1 2027
bullets.body: One trader argues markets are treating domestic AI infrastructure plays like AAOI as bearish despite their strategic importance, while the industry trends toward outsourcing transceivers to Asia. A bull-case revenue target of $471M/month by end-H1 2027 is cited against a current ~$13.4B valuation.

bullets.title: COHR has ~5 InP substrate suppliers; AXTI securing export permits
bullets.body: COHR is noted to have approximately five InP substrate suppliers and is not dependent on any single source, even as AXT (AXTI) obtains US export permits to ship to American companies' foreign facilities including COHR's Sweden fab. COHR also cited as capable of EPI manufacturing.

bullets.title: AMD claims 15/15 top Amazon CPU spots; Intel shut out
bullets.body: AMD's marketing chief boasts occupying all 15 of the top 15 best-selling CPU positions on Amazon, with Intel holding zero spots. The claim signals AMD's continued consumer PC momentum and ongoing INTC market share erosion.

bullets.title: Mag 7 divergence: only GOOGL and NVDA outperforming S&P 500 YTD 2026
bullets.body: Five of the seven Magnificent Seven stocks have underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date in 2026, with only Google and Nvidia in outperforming territory. This marks a sharp reversal from 2023-2024 when the cohort broadly led.

bullets.title: Retail rotating out of GOOG/AMZN/MSFT/META into SpaceX; rebalancing dynamics flagged
bullets.body: Social media commentary notes market participants selling large-cap tech (GOOG, AMZN, MSFT, META) to fund SpaceX IPO positions. Separately, institutions may be front-running a Nasdaq 100 rebalancing tied to SpaceX index inclusion, making attribution of the selloff unclear.

bullets.title: PPI prints hotter-than-expected at 1.1% MoM / 6.5% YoY; final demand goods biggest monthly jump on record
bullets.body: May PPI came in at +1.1% MoM (vs. +0.7% est.) and +6.5% YoY, the largest annual gain since November 2022. PPI final demand goods surged 2.8% in a single month, the biggest such jump on record; energy and gasoline (+23.4%) were the primary drivers. Core PPI at +0.4% MoM was slightly softer than the +0.5% estimate.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bps to 2.25% — first G7 central bank to raise rates since 2023 energy shock
bullets.body: The ECB raised its deposit facility rate to 2.25% (refi to 2.40%) in a unanimous decision, the first hike since 2023 and the first major central bank move in response to the Middle East energy shock. The ECB simultaneously cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.8% and raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.0%, while Lagarde flagged upside risks to inflation and warned against a pre-set rate path.

bullets.title: US jobless claims rise to 18-week high at 229K; labor market softening
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims came in at 229K vs. 220K estimate and 225K prior, hitting an 18-week high. Continuing claims also missed at 1.795M vs. 1.785M estimate. Largest increases were in Pennsylvania (+5.6K), California (+5.3K), and Minnesota (+5.3K).

bullets.title: Fed hike odds surge as inflation hits multi-year highs; new Chair Warsh faces Trump test
bullets.body: Market expectations for a Fed rate hike are rising with inflation hitting a three-year high. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh faces a choice between hiking to fight inflation or aligning with Trump's stated preference for lower rates; one commentator notes PPI at 6.5% and still rising makes a disinflation path difficult.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex volatility: free cash flow shift from cash to capex is a macro risk
bullets.body: Commentary notes that cash holdings carry near-zero volatility while AI capex introduces significant variance; hyperscalers are redirecting hundreds of billions of dollars in free cash flow toward AI infrastructure. Retail investors recorded their largest-ever IGV purchase near a recent market top, and the ETF has since declined ~15%.
